questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a place where I hopefully would be able to communicate with the hospital staff.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Poor organization at the host university and hospital.  I met all the language criteria in order to go to Spain. I thought since they didn't acquired a high level of spanish, I would be able to speak English while I was practicing Spanish. This wasn't the case. Not even the doctors really spoke English. I think the host university should make a language test prior to accepting the students in order to ensure that the student will be able to understand and learn at the hospital.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy to find relevant information on KUnet, but very difficult to find information on the Spanish websites. The coordinating professor was difficult to get in touch with.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I had written emails with the coordinating secretary at the hospital, but when I arrived she didn't really know who I was and what to do with me which was very frustrating. I found it very odd since we had a arranged a meeting the previous week. 
Once I got my rotations, it was easy enough.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got a contact I could write to from a previous exchange student. La Arena and Centro are nice areas to live in. Very easy to get a bus to the hospital from these areas.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try to find a room at at flat with other students. The city is small and the international community as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once I got nominated at KU I had to fill out an online application form.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The coordinating professor was very slow to reply to emails and sometimes I couldn't get a hold of him at all.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the rotations I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and don't stress too much over not getting a reply. It will all work out in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I didnt receive actual teaching but observed the patients at the hospital. Some of the doctors tried to explain some things, but in generel the level is not as high as I'm used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In my opinion, in Denmark the teaching is very focused on hands on. In Spain the students mostly just observe.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Internal medicine (medicina interna), Emergency (Urgencias), Pediatrics (Pediatria) and intensive care medicine (medicina intensiva)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Internal medicine and pediatrics were my best rotations. Very nice doctors and some that spoke english

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most of the activities happened in Oviedo (30 min by bus from Gijon). There were different trips arranged but did not have a lot of available spots (mostly due to COVID19).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Tapas tuesday's were a great way to meet others.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go surfing! And go Bilbao by bus or car (beautiful trip!)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is not that different from the danish but I had a lot if difficulty with the language barrier. my spanish improved a lot so it wasnt a problem in the end.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was quite difficult to meet local students since I had practical rotations at the hospital. But the doctors are friendly and the young doctors are happy to go for a drink.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The spanish food and openness on the streets. You say hi to people and talk to a lot of strangers all the time.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Learn spanish before coming! 
Dont expect to learn as much new stuff as you would at home. 
Enjoy your free time - the hospital is small and don't have a lot of patients so you have a lot of free time. 
Enjoy the sea and the nature - its beautiful!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I appreciate the Danish teaching system at lot more now than I did before.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
